questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which digital publication choice best fits students who need quick instructions for joining an online speech rehearsal?

answer.text: A. A long article about the value of rehearsal.

feedback.text: This does not fit the immediate audience need. Students need direct joining instructions, not an extended explanation.

answer.text: B. A decorative image with no link or steps.

feedback.text: This may look appealing, but it fails the purpose because the audience cannot use it to join the rehearsal.

answer.text: C. A full transcript of a past rehearsal.

feedback.text: This gives too much unrelated information. The format should help students act quickly.

answer.text: D. A short checklist with the link, time, and steps.

feedback.text: Correct. This format matches the audience need because it is clear, usable, and organized for quick action.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which choice best shows audience awareness in an email to families about a speech showcase?

answer.text: A. Use inside jokes from class.

feedback.text: This may confuse families. Audience awareness means selecting language that fits readers who were not in the classroom.

answer.text: B. Include a clear subject line, date, location, purpose, and contact information.

feedback.text: Correct. Families need practical event information presented in a respectful and easy-to-use way.

answer.text: C. Use vague wording so the message sounds casual.

feedback.text: Vague wording weakens communication. Families need clear details to understand the event and decide how to participate.

answer.text: D. Put the most important information at the end only.

feedback.text: This makes the message harder to use. Audience-aware organization places key details where readers can find them quickly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

A group is publishing slides for a presentation on interview preparation. Which choice best supports the speaker?

answer.text: A. Use brief headings and visuals that organize the speaker's explanation.

feedback.text: Correct. Slides should guide the audience and support what the speaker says aloud.

answer.text: B. Put the entire script on each slide.

feedback.text: This overloads the audience and weakens the role of the speaker. Slides should support, not replace, speech.

answer.text: C. Remove all visuals so the audience only listens.

feedback.text: This may reduce clarity. Useful visuals can help the audience follow key ideas when they are chosen carefully.

answer.text: D. Use unrelated images to make the slides more colorful.

feedback.text: Unrelated images distract from the message. Visuals should support the purpose and audience understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which design choice most supports accessibility?

answer.text: A. Tiny text and low contrast colors.

feedback.text: This makes the publication harder to read. Accessibility requires clear, readable design.

answer.text: B. Several animations on every line.

feedback.text: Too much animation can distract from the message. Design should support understanding, not create confusion.

answer.text: C. Hidden key details under decorative images.

feedback.text: This makes important information hard to find. Audience-aware design keeps key information visible.

answer.text: D. Readable text size, clear headings, and strong contrast.

feedback.text: Correct. These choices help the audience see, scan, and understand the digital publication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Before selecting a digital format, what should the communicator identify first?

answer.text: A. The audience and what they need to know first.

feedback.text: Correct. Audience and priority information should guide format, tone, organization, and design.

answer.text: B. The most decorative template available.

feedback.text: Decoration should not guide the communication plan. The audience's needs and purpose should come first.

answer.text: C. The longest possible message.

feedback.text: Length is not the goal. A strong publication includes enough information in a clear, useful form.

answer.text: D. The newest platform regardless of audience access.

feedback.text: A platform is only effective if the audience can access and use it. Popularity alone is not enough.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which publication plan best fits a school announcement about a career workshop?

answer.text: A. A complicated webpage with several unrelated sections.

feedback.text: This creates unnecessary work for the audience. A workshop announcement should be direct and easy to scan.

answer.text: B. A clear digital flyer with benefits, date, time, location, and sign-up link.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives the audience the information needed to understand the value and take action.

answer.text: C. A paragraph with no title, date, or sign-up information.

feedback.text: This fails the practical purpose. The audience needs key details to decide and participate.

answer.text: D. A visual collage with no explanation.

feedback.text: This may be decorative, but it does not communicate the event information clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Why should digital slides avoid placing every detail on one slide?

answer.text: A. It makes the speaker look too prepared.

feedback.text: Preparation is not the problem. The issue is whether the audience can process the information clearly.

answer.text: B. It prevents the speaker from using any evidence.

feedback.text: Crowded slides are not mainly about evidence use. The problem is overload and poor organization.

answer.text: C. It guarantees the audience will disagree.

feedback.text: Crowding can confuse an audience, but it does not guarantee disagreement.

answer.text: D. It can overload the audience and make the message harder to follow.

feedback.text: Correct. Slides should organize ideas so the audience can process the presentation step by step.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which tone best fits a digital invitation to community guests for a presentation showcase?

answer.text: A. Sarcastic and dismissive.

feedback.text: This tone would not fit community guests. It may damage trust and reduce clarity.

answer.text: B. Confusing and overly casual.

feedback.text: This does not support a public invitation. Guests need clear and respectful communication.

answer.text: C. Respectful, welcoming, and clear.

feedback.text: Correct. This tone fits the audience and purpose because it invites participation professionally.

answer.text: D. Secretive and vague.

feedback.text: This prevents the audience from understanding the event. A digital invitation should be clear and usable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which choice best explains why platform matters?

answer.text: A. The platform affects how the audience accesses, reads, and uses the message.

feedback.text: Correct. Digital publication requires choosing a format that fits how the audience will receive and act on the information.

answer.text: B. The platform matters only if the message is unimportant.

feedback.text: This is incorrect. Platform matters for important messages because access and clarity affect communication.

answer.text: C. The platform should always be the newest option.

feedback.text: New does not always mean useful. The platform should fit the audience and purpose.

answer.text: D. The platform replaces the need for clear organization.

feedback.text: No platform replaces organization. The message still needs clear structure and audience-aware design.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which choice best shows visual support for a spoken presentation?

answer.text: A. Slides that contain unrelated pictures.

feedback.text: Unrelated pictures distract from the speaker's message. Visuals should help the audience understand the content.

answer.text: B. Slides with clear headings that match the speaker's main points.

feedback.text: Correct. Clear headings guide the audience and support the speaker's organization.

answer.text: C. Slides with no connection to the speech order.

feedback.text: This creates confusion. Visual support should follow the structure of the spoken message.

answer.text: D. Slides that hide the main idea.

feedback.text: This works against communication. Visuals should make key ideas easier to follow.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which question best checks audience awareness?

answer.text: A. Does this design include every color I like?

feedback.text: Personal preference is not the main measure. Audience awareness focuses on what helps the audience understand.

answer.text: B. Can I make this message longer?

feedback.text: Longer is not automatically clearer. The message should be complete and usable for the audience.

answer.text: C. Did I choose the same format as everyone else?

feedback.text: Similarity is not enough. The format must fit the audience, purpose, and context.

answer.text: D. What does this audience need to know, and how can they use it easily?

feedback.text: Correct. This question connects audience needs with clear digital communication choices.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which publication choice is least audience-aware?

answer.text: A. A flyer with a clear title and sign-up link.

feedback.text: This is audience-aware because it helps readers understand and act on the message.

answer.text: B. An email with date, time, location, and purpose near the top.

feedback.text: This supports the audience by making essential information easy to find.

answer.text: C. A digital announcement with no purpose, no date, and no next step.

feedback.text: Correct. This fails audience awareness because readers cannot understand what to do or why the message matters.

answer.text: D. A slide with short headings and readable contrast.

feedback.text: This supports audience understanding because it is organized and visually clear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

How should visuals and speaker notes work together?

answer.text: A. Visuals should guide attention while speaker notes explain details aloud.

feedback.text: Correct. This balance helps the audience follow the message without crowding the digital product.

answer.text: B. Visuals should include the entire speech so notes are unnecessary.

feedback.text: This overloads the audience and weakens the speaker's role. Notes should guide spoken explanation.

answer.text: C. Speaker notes should ignore the visuals.

feedback.text: This creates a disconnect. Notes and visuals should support the same communication purpose.

answer.text: D. Visuals should be unrelated so the audience stays surprised.

feedback.text: Surprise is not the goal. Visuals should help the audience understand the presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which choice best revises a cluttered digital flyer?

answer.text: A. Add more fonts to make each line different.

feedback.text: More fonts often create clutter. A clear flyer uses consistent design to support reading.

answer.text: B. Move the date and sign-up link into tiny text.

feedback.text: This hides essential information. Audience-aware publication keeps action details visible.

answer.text: C. Add unrelated images to fill empty space.

feedback.text: Unrelated images distract from the purpose. Empty space can help readability.

answer.text: D. Use clear sections for benefits, date, location, and sign-up steps.

feedback.text: Correct. Clear sections organize the message so the audience can scan and act.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which statement best connects tone to audience?

answer.text: A. Tone should be the same for every audience.

feedback.text: This ignores audience awareness. Tone should fit the audience, purpose, and communication setting.

answer.text: B. Tone should match the relationship, purpose, and level of formality needed by the audience.

feedback.text: Correct. Audience-aware tone helps the message feel appropriate and understandable.

answer.text: C. Tone matters only in printed communication.

feedback.text: Tone matters in digital communication too because word choice affects how the audience receives the message.

answer.text: D. Tone should always be humorous.

feedback.text: Humor may not fit every audience or purpose. Tone should serve the communication goal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

What is the best reason to use brief slide headings?

answer.text: A. They make the presentation look finished even if ideas are unclear.

feedback.text: Headings cannot replace clear ideas. They should support organization and understanding.

answer.text: B. They let the speaker skip transitions.

feedback.text: Headings can support transitions, but the speaker still needs to guide the audience.

answer.text: C. They help the audience follow the speaker's organization.

feedback.text: Correct. Brief headings act as signposts so listeners can track the presentation.

answer.text: D. They make the presentation longer.

feedback.text: Length is not the goal. Headings support clarity and structure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which digital publication choice best supports a mixed audience of families, students, and staff?

answer.text: A. Clear language, essential details, and organization that does not assume background knowledge.

feedback.text: Correct. A mixed audience needs accessible wording and clearly organized information.

answer.text: B. Class-only abbreviations that students understand.

feedback.text: This may exclude families and staff. Audience-aware publication should not rely on insider language.

answer.text: C. A message that gives details only to one audience group.

feedback.text: This leaves other audience members without the information they need.

answer.text: D. A design with important details hidden in images.

feedback.text: This can reduce accessibility and clarity. Essential information should be readable and easy to find.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which choice best explains audience-aware organization?

answer.text: A. Put information in the order the creator thought of it.

feedback.text: This may not match audience needs. Organization should help the audience understand and act.

answer.text: B. Place the most important information where the audience can find it quickly.

feedback.text: Correct. Audience-aware organization prioritizes usability and clarity.

answer.text: C. Hide the main point to create suspense.

feedback.text: Suspense is not appropriate for most professional digital publications. The audience needs clarity.

answer.text: D. Use the same order for every communication product.

feedback.text: Different audiences and purposes may require different organization.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which slide choice best supports speaker credibility?

answer.text: A. A slide with unreadable text and no clear point.

feedback.text: This hurts credibility because the audience cannot follow the message.

answer.text: B. A slide full of unrelated jokes.

feedback.text: This distracts from the presentation purpose and may weaken the speaker's credibility.

answer.text: C. A slide with a clear claim, relevant visual, and organized support.

feedback.text: Correct. Clear and relevant design helps the audience trust and follow the speaker.

answer.text: D. A slide that contradicts what the speaker says.

feedback.text: This creates confusion and damages credibility.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which decision best matches purpose and platform?

answer.text: A. Use a long video when the audience only needs a deadline.

feedback.text: This does not fit the purpose. A deadline should be easy to find quickly.

answer.text: B. Use a hidden link when students need to sign up.

feedback.text: This creates a barrier. The platform should make action steps easy.

answer.text: C. Use a short announcement with a visible deadline and sign-up link.

feedback.text: Correct. This matches the purpose because the audience needs quick information and a clear next step.

answer.text: D. Use a complex format because it looks advanced.

feedback.text: Complexity is not the goal. The format should support understanding and action.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which choice best revises a message for a professional audience?

answer.text: A. Replace vague slang with clear, respectful, specific language.

feedback.text: Correct. Professional audiences need language that is clear, appropriate, and easy to act on.

answer.text: B. Add more jokes and remove the event details.

feedback.text: This weakens clarity and may not fit the setting. Professional tone should support the purpose.

answer.text: C. Use abbreviations only classmates know.

feedback.text: This excludes audience members who do not share the same background knowledge.

answer.text: D. Make the message less specific so it sounds relaxed.

feedback.text: Professional communication should be specific enough for the audience to understand and respond.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

What should a speaker do if a visual is interesting but unrelated to the message?

answer.text: A. Keep it because visuals are always helpful.

feedback.text: This is incorrect. Visuals help only when they support the message and audience understanding.

answer.text: B. Remove or replace it with a visual that supports the point.

feedback.text: Correct. A presentation visual should clarify or reinforce the message, not distract from it.

answer.text: C. Add several more unrelated visuals.

feedback.text: This increases distraction. More visuals do not improve communication if they do not fit the purpose.

answer.text: D. Stop explaining the point aloud.

feedback.text: The speaker still needs to explain ideas clearly. Visuals are support, not a replacement for communication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which choice best describes an effective digital publication?

answer.text: A. It is designed mainly to show the creator's favorite style.

feedback.text: Personal style should not be the main goal. The publication should serve audience, purpose, and message.

answer.text: B. It includes as much information as possible without organization.

feedback.text: This overloads the audience. Effective publication uses structure and selection.

answer.text: C. It presents the message clearly through a format, organization, and design that fit the audience.

feedback.text: Correct. Effective digital publication connects format, structure, and design to audience needs.

answer.text: D. It avoids all visuals and headings.

feedback.text: Visuals and headings can support clarity when they are relevant and accessible.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which statement best explains why "audience first" matters?

answer.text: A. It lets the communicator ignore the purpose.

feedback.text: Audience and purpose work together. Knowing the audience helps the communicator fulfill the purpose.

answer.text: B. It means the communicator should only choose popular formats.

feedback.text: Popularity is not enough. The format must fit how the audience will use the message.

answer.text: C. It removes the need for revision.

feedback.text: Audience awareness often requires revision. The communicator checks clarity, tone, and organization.

answer.text: D. It helps the communicator choose language, organization, and design that the audience can understand and use.

feedback.text: Correct. Audience-first planning shapes practical choices throughout the digital publication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L06_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which final check best supports a digital presentation product?

answer.text: A. Ask whether each visual, heading, and note supports the speaker's purpose and the audience's understanding.

feedback.text: Correct. This check connects design to presentation purpose and audience needs.

answer.text: B. Ask whether the product uses every available design feature.

feedback.text: Using every feature can create clutter. The best features are the ones that support the message.

answer.text: C. Ask whether the product hides the main point until the end.

feedback.text: This can confuse the audience. Presentation support should make the message easier to follow.

answer.text: D. Ask whether the product is longer than classmates' products.

feedback.text: Length does not prove quality. Clear audience-aware support is more important than size.
